meta.name: PhysAlts Space Frontier (0 to ~1 Light-Day)
meta.description: Humanity's spaceborne physics laboratories and deep-space probes mapped across logarithmic light-time zones from Low Earth Orbit (0.0014 light-sec) to Voyager 1 approaching 1 full light-day.

zones.label: Earth & LEO
zones.desc: Orbital physics labs, telescopes, and particle detectors around Earth

zones.label: The Moon
zones.desc: Lunar laser ranging, seismology, and far-side radio astrophysics (~1.28 light-sec)

zones.label: Sun & Inner Planets
zones.desc: Heliophysics, Mercury, Venus, and inner solar system probes

zones.label: Mars & Asteroids
zones.desc: Martian seismology, atmosphere physics, and asteroid sample returns (~12.5 light-min)

zones.label: Gas & Ice Giants
zones.desc: Jupiter, Saturn, magnetospheres, icy moons, and outer-planet physics

zones.label: Kuiper Belt to ~1 Light-Day
zones.desc: New Horizons, heliopause, and Voyager 1 & 2 reaching ~1 light-day from Earth

missions.name: ISS & Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer (AMS-02)
missions.agency: NASA / ESA / JAXA / Roscosmos / CSA / CERN
missions.summary: A 7.5-ton particle physics detector mounted on the International Space Station truss alongside the Cold Atom Lab, measuring over 200 billion cosmic rays above Earth's atmosphere.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Measured precision positron excess, cosmic-ray antiproton spectra, and heavy cosmic-ray isotopic ratios probing dark matter annihilation and pulsar acceleration.

missions.name: Hubble Space Telescope (HST)
missions.summary: A 2.4-meter optical, ultraviolet, and near-infrared space telescope operating above atmospheric distortion for over three decades.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Pinned down the Hubble constant and cosmic age (~13.8 Gyr), imaged the Hubble Deep Fields, confirmed supermassive black holes in galaxy cores, and measured exoplanet atmospheric transmission.

missions.name: Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope
missions.summary: All-sky high-energy gamma-ray observatory surveying photons from 8 keV to over 300 GeV from pulsars, blazars, and cosmic explosions.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Discovered the giant 50,000-light-year Fermi Bubbles above the Milky Way core, co-detected the GW170817 binary neutron star kilonova gamma-ray burst, and set stringent Lorentz-invariance limits.

missions.name: Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE)
missions.summary: Three grazing-incidence X-ray telescopes measuring the linear polarization of X-rays emitted by extreme magnetic fields and spacetime around neutron stars and black holes.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Mapped magnetic field geometry in supernova remnants, magnetars, and blazar jets, testing quantum electrodynamics vacuum birefringence in strong magnetic fields.

missions.name: XMM-Newton X-ray Observatory
missions.summary: ESA's high-throughput X-ray spectroscopy flagship with 174 nested gold-coated nickel mirror shells studying hot plasma in galaxy clusters and active galactic nuclei.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Measured relativistic iron K-alpha line broadening near spinning black holes and mapped hot baryonic gas across the cosmic web.

missions.name: Chandra X-ray Observatory
missions.summary: NASA's sub-arcsecond X-ray flagship flying a 64-hour elliptical orbit up to a third of the way to the Moon to avoid Earth's radiation belts.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Provided decisive empirical evidence for dark matter in the Bullet Cluster collision, imaged neutron star cooling superfluids, and traced black-hole feedback in galaxy clusters.

missions.name: Apollo 11–17 Lunar Laser Ranging & ALSEP
missions.summary: Passive corner-cube laser retroreflectors deployed by Apollo 11, 14, and 15 astronauts (plus Soviet Lunokhods) alongside historic ALSEP lunar seismometers and magnetometers.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Measures the Earth–Moon distance to millimeter precision, verifying Einstein's Strong Equivalence Principle, constraining any drift in Newton's G, and revealing the Moon's 3.8 cm/yr tidal recession.

missions.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO)
missions.summary: High-resolution lunar mapping and radiation-physics orbiter producing global topographic, thermal, and neutron maps of the Moon.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Measured the coldest known natural surface temperatures in the solar system (<30 K) inside permanently shadowed south-polar craters and mapped lunar water-ice signatures and cosmic-ray albedo.

missions.name: Chandrayaan-3 (Vikram & Pragyan)
missions.summary: First mission to achieve a soft landing near the lunar south pole, performing in-situ thermophysical, plasma, seismic, and laser-breakdown elemental physics experiments.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Measured the first steep subsurface thermal gradient in southern high-latitude regolith, detected sparse lunar near-surface ionosphere plasma, and confirmed sulfur via LIBS.

missions.name: Chang'e-4 & Yutu-2
missions.body: The Moon (Far Side — Von Kármán Crater)
missions.summary: First soft landing on the radio-quiet far side of the Moon, relayed via the Queqiao Earth–Moon L2 satellite to conduct low-frequency radio astronomy and deep regolith radar sounding.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Performed ultra-long-wavelength radio observations shielded from terrestrial RFI, measured lunar surface neutral-atom radiation doses, and profiled 40 m of subsurface ejecta stratigraphy.

missions.name: Artemis Program & Lunar Gateway
missions.body: The Moon (Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit & South Pole)
missions.summary: Following Artemis II's historic April 2026 crewed lunar flyby, Artemis III and Lunar Gateway establish humanity's first deep-space orbital station in cislunar space for lunar seismology, radiation monitoring, and far-side cosmology.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Will measure deep-space solar energetic particles outside Earth's magnetosphere (HERMES & ERSA) and deploy updated single-prism retroreflectors for sub-millimeter gravity tests.

missions.name: Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO)
missions.summary: Positioned 1.5 million km sunward at Lagrange L1 for an uninterrupted view of the Sun's interior acoustic waves, corona, and solar wind.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Mapped the Sun's internal differential rotation and tachocline via helioseismology, monitored coronal mass ejections across nearly three solar cycles, and discovered over 5,000 sungrazing comets.

missions.name: Planck Space Observatory
missions.summary: Cryogenic microwave space telescope cooled to 0.1 K that mapped the entire Cosmic Microwave Background sky in nine frequency bands from 30 to 857 GHz.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Delivered the benchmark measurement of cosmic parameters: 68.5% dark energy, 26.5% dark matter, 4.9% ordinary matter, flat geometry, and tight constraints on primordial inflation.

missions.name: Gaia Astrometry Observatory
missions.summary: Dual-telescope microarcsecond astrometry mission that charted the 3D positions, parallaxes, and velocities of nearly two billion stars in the Milky Way (science observations ended Jan 2025; spacecraft retired Mar 2025; DR4/DR5 releases ongoing).
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Uncovered the ancient Gaia-Enceladus galactic merger, discovered dormant stellar-mass black holes (Gaia BH1–BH3), and tested general-relativistic light deflection across the whole sky.

missions.name: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)
missions.summary: Humanity's largest space telescope—a 6.5 m gold-coated segmented infrared observatory shielded behind a five-layer tennis-court-sized sunshield at L2.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Revealed unexpectedly luminous galaxies at redshift z > 14 (<300 Myr after the Big Bang), detected CO₂ and CH₄ in exoplanet atmospheres, and sharpened measurements of the Hubble tension.

missions.name: Euclid Dark Universe Telescope
missions.summary: Wide-field 1.2 m optical and near-infrared space telescope mapping weak gravitational lensing and baryon acoustic oscillations across one-third of the extragalactic sky.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Constructing a 3D cosmic map of billions of galaxies out to 10 billion light-years to test whether dark energy is a cosmological constant or modified gravity.

missions.name: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
missions.summary: A 2.4 m wide-field infrared survey observatory launched on August 30, 2026 to Sun–Earth L2 with 100× Hubble's field of view plus an active coronagraph for direct exoplanet imaging.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Will measure dark energy via weak lensing and Type Ia supernovae while discovering thousands of cold and rogue exoplanets through gravitational microlensing.

missions.name: LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna)
missions.summary: Three drag-free spacecraft housing free-falling gold-platinum test masses in a 2.5-million-km laser interferometer triangle following Earth's orbit around the Sun.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Will detect millihertz gravitational waves from supermassive black hole coalescences, extreme mass-ratio inspirals, Galactic white dwarf binaries, and possible cosmological phase transitions.

missions.name: Solar Orbiter (SolO)
missions.summary: Inclined heliophysics explorer using Venus gravity assists to climb out of the ecliptic plane and capture the first direct images of the Sun's magnetic poles.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Discovered miniature 'campfire' nanoflares heating the corona and directly linked in-situ solar-wind plasma streams back to their magnetic footpoints on the photosphere.

missions.name: BepiColombo
missions.body: Mercury (0.39 AU from Sun; ~0.85 AU avg from Earth)
missions.summary: Dual-orbiter European-Japanese mission (MPO & Mio) that entered Mercury orbit on November 21, 2026 via weak stability capture to map its huge iron core, active dynamo magnetosphere, and perform precision tests of general relativity.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Will measure Mercury's relativistic perihelion advance and Shapiro time delay to test the PPN gravity parameters γ and β while probing solar-wind magnetosphere coupling.

missions.name: Parker Solar Probe
missions.body: Solar Corona (0.046 AU from Sun; ~1.0 AU from Earth)
missions.summary: The fastest human-made object in history (~692,000 km/h), plunging through the Sun's outer atmosphere within 6.1 million km of the solar surface behind a carbon-composite heat shield.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Became the first spacecraft to cross the Alfvén critical surface into the magnetically dominated corona, uncovering magnetic 'switchbacks' and interchange reconnection powering the fast solar wind.
instruments: SWEAP Solar Wind Electrons Alphas & Protons

missions.name: Hayabusa2
missions.summary: Returned 5.4 grams of pristine carbonaceous asteroid regolith from Ryugu to Earth in 2020 after firing an explosive copper impactor to excavate subsurface material; now cruising toward asteroid 1998 KY26.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Revealed low-cohesion rubble-pile impact mechanics in microgravity and delivered amino-acid-rich primitive solar-nebula samples unaltered by terrestrial atmosphere.

missions.name: OSIRIS-REx / OSIRIS-APEX
missions.summary: Collected 121.6 grams of asteroid Bennu and delivered the sample capsule to Utah in 2023, continuing as OSIRIS-APEX to study tidal-torque physics during Apophis's 2029 close Earth flyby.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Directly measured the Yarkovsky thermal recoil force altering Bennu's orbit, observed spontaneous particle-ejection plumes, and found water-bearing clays and prebiotic organics.

missions.name: Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity)
missions.summary: Nuclear-powered rover ascending Mount Sharp inside Gale Crater with an onboard analytical chemistry, radiation-physics, and laser-spectroscopy laboratory.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Quantified interplanetary and Martian surface ionizing radiation doses (RAD), detected seasonal methane variations, and documented ancient lacustrine habitability.

missions.name: Mars 2020 (Perseverance & Ingenuity)
missions.summary: Core-sampling astrobiology and atmospheric-physics rover paired with the Ingenuity rotorcraft, which proved powered aerodynamic flight in Mars's 1% CO₂ atmosphere across 72 flights.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Demonstrated solid-oxide electrolysis producing O₂ from Martian CO₂ (MOXIE), recorded the dual speed of sound in CO₂ with microphones, and mapped subsurface strata via radar.

missions.name: InSight Mars Seismology Lander
missions.summary: Dedicated geophysical observatory that placed an ultra-sensitive broadband seismometer directly on the Martian surface to listen to the planet's deep interior (2018–2022).
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Detected over 1,300 marsquakes and meteoroid impacts, directly measuring the thickness of the Martian crust (~24–72 km), mantle structure, and a liquid iron-alloy core (~1,650–1,830 km radius).
instruments: RISE Rotation & Interior Structure Radio Science

missions.name: DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test)
missions.summary: Humanity's first full-scale planetary defense kinetic-impactor experiment, colliding autonomously with asteroid moonlet Dimorphos at 6.1 km/s in September 2022 (impact at 0.073 AU from Earth).
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Shortened Dimorphos's 11h 55m orbit by 33 minutes—demonstrating a momentum enhancement factor β ≈ 3.6 driven by high-velocity ejecta recoil.

missions.name: Psyche Mission to 16 Psyche
missions.summary: Solar-electric Hall-thruster spacecraft traveling to the metal-rich asteroid 16 Psyche (arrival 2029) while demonstrating Deep Space Optical Communications (DSOC) laser links across interplanetary distances.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Achieved record-breaking deep-space laser telemetry at hundreds of millions of km and will probe whether 16 Psyche is the exposed nickel-iron core of a differentiated planetesimal.

missions.name: Juno Jupiter Polar Orbiter
missions.summary: Solar-powered polar orbiter skimming within 4,200 km of Jupiter's cloud tops to probe its metallic-hydrogen interior, intense auroral radiation belts, and Galilean moons.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Discovered Jupiter's 'fuzzy' diluted core via precision Doppler gravity harmonics, mapped asymmetric non-dipolar magnetic fields, and revealed polygonal polar cyclones and 3,000 km deep jet streams.

missions.name: JUICE (Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer)
missions.body: En Route to Jupiter & Ganymede (5.2 AU)
missions.summary: ESA flagship mission arriving at Jupiter in 2031 to perform detailed flybys of Europa and Callisto before entering the first-ever orbit around Ganymede.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Will characterize Ganymede's unique intrinsic planetary magnetic dipole, measure subsurface liquid-water oceans via magnetic induction and ice-penetrating radar, and study tidal heating physics.

missions.name: Europa Clipper
missions.body: En Route to Jupiter / Europa (5.2 AU)
missions.summary: NASA's largest planetary spacecraft, arriving at Jupiter in 2030 to execute nearly 50 low-altitude flybys through Jupiter's extreme radiation belts to investigate Europa's global salty ocean.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Will measure Europa's ice-shell thickness, induced magnetic ocean salinity and depth, tidal flexing love numbers, and sputtered surface chemistry via mass spectrometry.

missions.name: Cassini–Huygens
missions.summary: Spent 13 years orbiting Saturn (2004–2017) and landed the ESA Huygens probe on Titan, concluding with Grand Finale plunges between Saturn and its rings.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Performed the highest-precision Shapiro gravitational time-delay test of general relativity (γ − 1 < 2.3 × 10⁻⁵), discovered hydrothermal water plumes erupting from Enceladus, and revealed liquid methane seas on Titan.

missions.name: Dragonfly Titan Rotorcraft
missions.summary: Nuclear-powered dual-quadcopter lander slated to launch in 2028 and arrive at Titan in 2034, flying tens of kilometers across organic dunes and impact craters in Titan's dense 1.45-bar nitrogen atmosphere.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Will measure Titan's seismic interior and subsurface ocean, sample prebiotic organic chemistry with a laser mass spectrometer, and test cryogenic aerodynamics.

missions.name: New Horizons
missions.summary: First spacecraft to explore the Pluto–Charon system (2015) and contact-binary Kuiper Belt object Arrokoth (2019), now measuring outer heliosphere dust, plasma, and the dark cosmic optical background.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Uncovered active nitrogen-ice convection glaciers on Pluto, directly measured the faint extragalactic Cosmic Optical Background free of inner-solar-system zodiacal light, and tracked pickup-ion acceleration.
instruments: SDC Venetia Burney Student Dust Counter

missions.name: Voyager 2
missions.summary: The only spacecraft to visit all four giant planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune), having crossed the heliopause into interstellar space in November 2018.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Discovered tilted offset magnetic dynamos at Uranus and Neptune and provided the first direct in-situ plasma density and temperature measurements across the heliopause boundary.

missions.name: Voyager 1
missions.summary: Humanity's farthest ambassador—racing outward at ~3.6 AU/year in the local interstellar medium after crossing the heliopause in August 2012, officially reaching 1 full light-day (~173.1 AU, 25.9 billion km) from Earth on November 18, 2026.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Measured the abrupt jump in galactic cosmic rays and interstellar plasma electron density beyond the Sun's magnetic bubble, and detected persistent interstellar plasma-wave 'hum' driven by solar shock waves.
